details:
EMBER Spacefire is an interactive research dashboard that makes NASA’s spacecraft fire-safety research easier to explore and interpret. It brings together findings from Saffire flame-spread experiments, FLEX droplet-combustion studies, and SAME smoke-detection research. Users can explore the studies, view charts, download CSV files, follow links to original NASA sources, and read a mission-focused summary of the evidence.

The dashboard’s benefit is that it turns research spread across technical reports and experiment records into an accessible starting point for asking fire-safety questions relevant to future Moon and Mars missions. It highlights evidence about material flammability, combustion and extinction, and smoke detection to help researchers, students, and mission planners identify topics for further investigation. It is a research and learning aid, not a flight-safety certification or operational procedure.

We built the dashboard with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG charts, and CSV data. We use GitHub to store the project and Firebase Hosting to publish it. No special hardware is required. ChatGPT and Claude assisted with code, interface text, evidence synthesis, and transcription or integration of published values. The dashboard identifies this assistance and links findings to their sources; no AI model runs live predictions in the app.

The project’s creative approach is to connect each experiment to a practical mission question, helping users move from scientific evidence to possible design considerations. We considered source traceability, experimental conditions, and the limits of comparing different fuels, geometries, pressures, flows, and gravity conditions. Approximate chart values are labelled, and relevance scores are illustrative navigation aids—not probabilities, risk predictions, or NASA ratings.
